item.title: Nasinu Women go back to the drawing board ahead of Pio Bosco Trophy defence
item.description: Subrails Pio Bosco Trophy holders Nasinu Women’s rugby tea m have returned to the drawing board this week as they prepare to defend their title following a hard-fought 44-36 victory over defending champions Namosi last week. Nasinu team captain, Sera Bolatini says the team has stepped up preparations, knowing that defending the trophy will not be easy.
item.content:encoded:
Subrails Pio Bosco Trophy holders Nasinu Women’s rugby tea m have returned to the drawing board this week as they prepare to defend their title following a hard-fought 44-36 victory over defending champions Namosi last week.

Nasinu team captain, Sera Bolatini says the team has stepped up preparations, knowing that defending the trophy will not be easy.

Bolatini , who led from the front with powerful runs and impressive offloads, says the team has identified areas that need improvement following their closely contested match against Namosi.

She says they have learned from their mistakes and are working on their weaknesses to deliver a stronger performance this week.

Bolatini is confident her players will maintain their winning momentum in their upcoming match.

Nasinu will face Suva this week with the time and venue to be confirmed.

item.title: Getting to know Flying Fijians players an exciting challenge – White
item.description: Navitalai Naivalurua · 17/11/2026 One of the challenges facing Jake White as head coach of the FIJI Water Flying Fijians is getting to know and understand the players in his squad.
item.content:encoded:
Navitalai Naivalurua · 17/11/2026

One of the challenges facing Jake White as head coach of the FIJI Water Flying Fijians is getting to know and understand the players in his squad.

Following Fiji's 43-15 loss to Ireland in the Nations Championship on Sunday, White says he is still trying to find out who's who in the team.

He says it is quite an exciting challenge for him.

In the post-match press conference, White says Fiji are still caught between the way the game should be played and the way they have historically played.

The Flying Fijians are continuing their preparations for their final Nations Championship match against Italy this week, which kicks off at 4.40am on Sunday.

In other matches this Sunday, England will face the All Blacks, while Scotland will meet Japan, with both matches kicking off at 2.10am.

Ireland will face South Africa at 4.40am.

item.title: Police target back-to-back Sukuna Bowl victory against Army
item.description: The Police rugby team is intensifying preparations for this Friday’s Vodafone Ratu Sukuna Bowl clash against Army as they aim to defend their title and secure back-to-back victories. Speaking to fijivillage Sports, Acting Assistant Commissioner of Police Administration Jovilisi Leweniqila says the team is preparing well so far.
item.content:encoded:
The Police rugby team is intensifying preparations for this Friday’s Vodafone Ratu Sukuna Bowl clash against Army as they aim to defend their title and secure back-to-back victories.

Speaking to fijivillage Sports, Acting Assistant Commissioner of Police Administration Jovilisi Leweniqila says the team is preparing well so far.

He says it is not easy to defend the trophy, and they are anticipating a tough game this Friday.

Leweniqila says they have a few players from the Skipper Cup Competition, and they are banking on their experience to help the force this week.

He says the players are in camp and the main rugby team is camping in Nadroga and will arrive in Suva on Wednesday.

Leweniqila says they will try their best to win it for the 5th straight year this year.

Police are defending the Sukuna Bowl after beating Army last year 26-10 in Labasa.

Police will face Army at 4pm this Friday at HFC Stadium.

item.title: Historic Ra-Nadroga clash unites community and keeps youths away from drugs and HIV - Duaniwai
item.description: The historic match between Ra and current Farebrother Trophy holders Nadroga brought the people of Ra together and encouraged young people to focus on rugby, keeping them away from HIV and drugs. Speaking after the game at Narauyabale Ground, Rakiraki Town Council Special Administrator Peni Duaniwai says hosting a big match in Ra was a blessing for the Province as the game united the people and br
item.content:encoded:
The historic match between Ra and current Farebrother Trophy holders Nadroga brought the people of Ra together and encouraged young people to focus on rugby, keeping them away from HIV and drugs.

Speaking after the game at Narauyabale Ground, Rakiraki Town Council Special Administrator Peni Duaniwai says hosting a big match in Ra was a blessing for the Province as the game united the people and brought happiness and joy to a community whose members had only dreamed of hosting major sporting events in their province.

He says business was booming, with food vendors making money to support their families and livelihoods during the big match.

Duaniwai says senior citizens in the province who couldn't travel long distances to Suva or Nadi, could just go to Narauyabale Ground and watch their own team take on reigning champions Nadroga.

He says the day would go down in history as one of the most unforgettable moments in rugby, as it brought the people of Ra and Nadroga together.

Tailevu will challenge Nadroga next for the Farebrother Trophy match at Lawaqa Park in Sigatoka.

The date of the challenge will be confirmed soon.

item.title: Disappointing weekend for Southern Hemisphere teams in Nations Championship
item.description: Navitalai Naivalurua · 16/11/2026 It was a disappointing weekend for Southern Hemisphere rugby teams as four of the five teams suffered defeats in their Nations Championship matches.
item.content:encoded:
Navitalai Naivalurua · 16/11/2026

It was a disappointing weekend for Southern Hemisphere rugby teams as four of the five teams suffered defeats in their Nations Championship matches.

South Africa went down 21-19 to France on Saturday, while the All Blacks lost 35-28 to Wales on Sunday.

The FIJI Water Flying Fijians lost 43-15 to Ireland, while the Wallabies went down 15-12 to Scotland this morning.

Argentina was the only Southern Hemisphere team to secure a win, defeating Italy 19-14.

In this Sunday's Nations Championship matches, England will face the All Blacks, while Scotland will meet Japan, with both matches kicking off at 2.10am.

The Flying Fijians will take on Italy, while Ireland will face South Africa, with both matches scheduled for 4.40am.

France will face Argentina, while Wales will play the Wallabies, with both matches kicking off at 8.10am.
